objectives: Engage AI ethics + existential risk — Bostrom 2014 *Superintelligence*, Russell *Human Compatible*, Christiano alignment, Floridi information ethics.
Survey experimental philosophy — Knobe, Stich, Machery cross-cultural intuitions, xphi.
Map LLMs + philosophy + the future of the discipline — Chalmers on LLM consciousness, philosophy as engineering field.

slides.title: AI ethics + existential risk — Bostrom, Russell, Christiano, Floridi
slides.body:
The 21st-century frontier of philosophy is increasingly defined by **AI ethics + AI safety + information ethics + algorithmic society**.

**Nick Bostrom, ***Superintelligence: Paths, Dangers, Strategies*** (2014)** — the founding text of modern AI-existential-risk philosophy.
- **Superintelligence**: an intellect that greatly exceeds humans in every relevant cognitive domain.
- **Paths to superintelligence**: AI, whole-brain emulation, biological cognitive enhancement, brain-computer interfaces, networks + organizations.
- **Recursive self-improvement** + **intelligence explosion** (cf. I. J. Good 1965 — 'an ultraintelligent machine could design even better machines') — the possibility of a fast takeoff.
- **Orthogonality thesis**: intelligence + final goals are (mostly) orthogonal — any level of intelligence is compatible with any (relatively coherent) set of goals. A superintelligent paperclip maximizer is logically consistent.
- **Instrumental convergence**: most final goals imply convergent instrumental sub-goals — self-preservation, goal-content integrity, cognitive enhancement, resource acquisition.
- **Control problem + value-loading**: how to design a superintelligence whose values + behavior reliably serve human interests? Coherent extrapolated volition (CEV — Yudkowsky-inspired), indirect normativity, ML-based value learning, corrigibility.
- Bostrom's book is required reading in AI safety + policy + has shaped DeepMind + OpenAI + Anthropic + UK AI Safety Institute + Future of Humanity Institute (Oxford, closed 2024). Critics: Etzioni, Brooks, LeCun — argue the timeline + threat model are overstated. Defenders: the *paths-and-dangers* framing has held up across multiple AI generations.

**Stuart Russell, ***Human Compatible: Artificial Intelligence and the Problem of Control*** (2019)** — co-author of the canonical AI textbook *AIRMA* (Russell + Norvig 1995-2020).
- **Standard model of AI** (optimize a fixed objective) is fundamentally wrong because: (a) we don't know our true objectives; (b) optimizing an incorrect objective with sufficient capability is catastrophic (King-Midas problem).
- **Three principles for beneficial AI**: (1) the machine's *only* objective is to maximize the realization of human preferences; (2) the machine is *initially uncertain* about what those preferences are; (3) the *ultimate source* of information about human preferences is human behavior + statement.
- **Cooperative inverse reinforcement learning (CIRL)** + **assistance games** as a formal framework — the AI does not assume it knows the objective + treats the human as a source of preference information.
- Russell argues we must redesign AI from the ground up around this *beneficial-AI* framework before we have superintelligence. *Human Compatible* is the most practically engaged + technically grounded recent treatment + has informed major-lab safety + alignment programs.

**Paul Christiano + the alignment program**:
- ***Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences*** (Christiano + Leike + Brown + Martic + Legg + Amodei 2017) — pioneered **RLHF** (reinforcement learning from human feedback), now the dominant alignment technique for LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini).
- **Constitutional AI** (Anthropic — Bai + Kadavath + Kundu + Askell + ... 2022) — using AI feedback + a constitution to train safer + more honest assistants. Now a central paradigm.
- **AI safety via debate** (Irving + Christiano + Amodei 2018); **iterated amplification + distillation** (Christiano 2018+); **scalable oversight**; **interpretability** (Olah + Anthropic + DeepMind Distill program + circuits); **mechanistic interpretability** (Anthropic 2022+; **Elhage + Olsson + Olah + Henighan** monosemanticity + scaling 2023-24).
- Christiano left OpenAI to found **Alignment Research Center (ARC)**; later joined **US AI Safety Institute** as Head of Safety (2024).
- **Eliezer Yudkowsky + MIRI** + the LessWrong / rationalist community + **Future of Humanity Institute** (Oxford) + **Center for Human-Compatible AI** (Berkeley, Russell) + **Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepMind, Redwood** alignment teams.

**Toby Ord, *The Precipice* (2020)** + **Will MacAskill, *What We Owe the Future* (2022)** — **longtermism**. The view that *positively shaping the long-term future is among our top moral priorities*. Estimating existential risk in this century: Ord puts AI risk at ~1/10, totalcomprehensive existential risk at ~1/6. Population-ethics + moral uncertainty foundations (cf. Parfit lesson 5). Hugely influential — + controversial (FTX-EA crisis 2022 strained the movement).

**Luciano Floridi + information ethics**:
- ***The Philosophy of Information*** (2011); ***The Ethics of Information*** (2013); ***Information: A Very Short Introduction*** (2010); ***The Logic of Information*** (2019); ***The Ethics of AI*** (with Cowls + others 2022).
- **Information ethics**: information is the central category of contemporary ethics; agents are *informational organisms* (*inforgs*); the *infosphere* is the ontological + ethical environment.
- Four principles for AI ethics (Floridi-Cowls 2019 *AI4People*): **beneficence, non-maleficence, autonomy, justice + explicability**. Inspired EU + national AI ethics frameworks.
- **AI ethics field** — Floridi at Oxford + Bologna, Yale + Princeton centers, MIT Media Lab, Stanford HAI, Mila ethics, Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepMind responsibility teams. Now a substantial subdiscipline integrating philosophy + CS + law + policy + governance.

**Broader algorithmic + AI ethics**:
- **Cathy O'Neil *Weapons of Math Destruction* (2016)**, **Virginia Eubanks *Automating Inequality* (2018)**, **Ruha Benjamin *Race After Technology* (2019)**, **Safiya Noble *Algorithms of Oppression* (2018)**, **Shoshana Zuboff *Surveillance Capitalism* (2019)** — sociology + critical race + STS engagement with algorithmic systems (cross-ref P63 lesson 8).
- **Joy Buolamwini + Timnit Gebru *Gender Shades* (2018)** — algorithmic audit revealing 34-point accuracy gaps in commercial facial recognition.
- **Bender + Gebru + McMillan-Major + Mitchell 'Stochastic Parrots' (FAccT 2021)** — early critical philosophy of LLMs.
- **Algorithmic fairness** literature (Dwork, Kleinberg, Chouldechova, Friedler, Barocas-Hardt-Narayanan *Fairness and Machine Learning* 2019) — formal philosophy + CS.
- **AI + value alignment + governance**: Krakovna + DeepMind safety + Anthropic Responsible Scaling + EU AI Act 2024 + Bletchley + Seoul + Paris AI Safety Summits.

The philosophy of AI is now one of the most active + consequential subfields + integrates ethics + epistemology + philosophy of mind + political philosophy.

slides.title: Experimental philosophy — Knobe, Stich, Machery, cross-cultural intuitions
slides.body:
**Experimental philosophy** (***xphi***) emerged in the early 2000s as a movement to bring empirical methods — surveys, behavioral experiments, cross-cultural studies, statistics — to bear on traditional philosophical questions, particularly the *intuitions* on which much of analytic philosophy has relied.

**The motivating worry**: analytic philosophy frequently invokes 'our intuitions' about cases (Gettier, trolley problems, Twin Earth, Mary's Room) to support or refute theories. But whose intuitions? Are these intuitions stable across cultures, classes, genders, ages, philosophical training? If not, what is their evidential weight?

**Joshua Knobe + Shaun Nichols, *Experimental Philosophy* (2008) + Knobe + Nichols + Schaffer + Sosa et al. ongoing program**. Pioneered the empirical turn.

**The Knobe Effect (Joshua Knobe 2003, 'Intentional Action and Side Effects in Ordinary Language')** — an empirical finding that became the founding result of xphi:
- Vignette: a CEO's decision will (a) **harm** the environment as a side effect of a profit-seeking plan, or (b) **help** the environment as a side effect. The CEO knows + says he doesn't care either way.
- People judge the *harming* CEO as having acted *intentionally* (~80%) but the *helping* CEO as having acted *unintentionally* (~20%) — even though the structural relation to the side effect is identical.
- Suggests intentionality attributions are *normatively laden* — intuitions about intentional action are partly *moral* judgments, not purely descriptive cognitive judgments.
- Replicated 100+ times + extended to causation, knowledge, free will, weakness of will, character traits — the *side-effect effect* generalizes.
- Generated a major literature in moral psychology + action theory + philosophy of language.

**Stephen Stich + Kim + Cova + others — cross-cultural intuitions**.
- **Weinberg, Nichols + Stich, 'Normativity and Epistemic Intuitions' (2001)** — *intuitions about Gettier cases differ by ethnicity + socioeconomic status*. East Asian + Indian respondents were more likely to attribute knowledge to the Gettier subject than Western respondents. *Massive* implications for an analytic epistemology that has treated Gettier-case intuitions as universal data.
- Later replication efforts (Machery + Kim + Mallon + Stich; Knobe; Cova et al. 'Estimating the Reproducibility of Experimental Philosophy' 2018) found *some* effects are robust, others not. The replication-crisis lessons of psychology apply.

**Edouard Machery + Kim + Mallon + Nichols + Stich, ***Doing without Concepts*** (2009)**; **'Semantics, cross-cultural style' (Machery et al. 2004)**.
- *Kripke-Putnam intuitions about reference may not be universal*. Asked to consider the **Gödel case** (someone other than Gödel actually proved incompleteness; what does 'Gödel' refer to?), Western respondents tend to be Kripkeans (causal-historical chain — refers to the actual Gödel); East Asian respondents more frequently give descriptivist answers (refers to whoever proved the theorem). If reference intuitions vary by culture, Kripke's master argument (lesson 2) is on shakier footing.
- Machery, ***Philosophy Within Its Proper Bounds*** (2017) — radical conclusion: the **method-of-cases** is unreliable + philosophy should rebuild itself around different methods.

**Other major xphi findings + topics**:
- **Free will + responsibility** (Nichols + Knobe 2007, Nahmias et al.): folk intuitions are *mostly compatibilist*, contra philosophical assumptions; intuitions vary with the level of abstraction (abstract questions → incompatibilist; concrete cases → compatibilist).
- **Causation + transitivity** (Hitchcock, Knobe, Schaffer) — folk causal judgments are normatively + pragmatically structured.
- **Personal identity** (Nichols + Bruno; Strohminger + Nichols 2014 *The Essential Moral Self*) — moral character is central to perceived identity; transformations of moral character feel like loss of self more than memory loss.
- **Moral judgment** + psychopath studies (Schaich-Borg, Greene 2008 *fMRI* + trolley): different neural systems for personal vs impersonal harm.
- **Cross-cultural moral philosophy**: Henrich + Heine + Norenzayan *The Weirdest People in the World* (2010) — most psychology + much philosophy has sampled from **WEIRD** populations (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, Democratic). Major implications.
- **Conceptual engineering** (Cappelen *Fixing Language* 2018; Burgess + Plunkett + Sterken *Conceptual Engineering* 2020) — should philosophy *engineer* concepts to better fit empirical + normative aims, rather than merely *analyze* them?
- **Philosophy + cognitive science integration**: pervasive — moral psychology (Haidt, Greene), psychology of religion, philosophy of psychiatry (Murphy, Kingma), embodied + extended cognition (Clark, Wheeler, Noë).

**Critiques of xphi**:
- **Methodological concerns**: surveys ≠ careful philosophical reflection; respondents may misread vignettes; statistical power; replication.
- **Expertise defense** (Williamson, Devitt): philosophical intuitions of *trained philosophers* may be more reliable than folk intuitions — analogous to expert intuitions in physics or chess. Studies of expert vs novice intuitions (Knobe; Schwitzgebel; Cova et al.) are mixed.
- **What follows from variation?** Even if intuitions vary, they may still be evidence — just heavily weighted by other considerations. Or variation may signal that a question is *contested*, not that it lacks an answer.

**The legacy**: xphi has irreversibly changed how analytic philosophy engages intuitions. The PhilPapers Survey (Bourget + Chalmers 2009, 2020) tracks philosophers' views statistically — a meta-empirical turn in the discipline itself. Many philosophy programs now include empirical-methods training; **philosophy + cognitive science + moral psychology + behavioral ethics** are pervasively integrated.

slides.title: LLMs + philosophy + the future of the discipline
slides.body:
The arrival of **large language models (LLMs)** + frontier AI in the early 2020s has reshaped philosophical inquiry — both as object of study + as tool.

**LLMs as object of philosophy**.

**David Chalmers, 'Could a Large Language Model Be Conscious?' (*Boston Review* 2023; expanded in *Journal of Philosophy of AI* + multiple venues)** — the most systematic philosophical treatment of LLM consciousness.
- Chalmers takes the question seriously, assesses present-generation LLMs (GPT-4 vintage at time of writing) against leading theories (GWT — Baars/Dehaene; IIT — Tononi; higher-order theories; global broadcasting). Concludes: *probably not conscious* (lack of recurrence + integrated workspace + embodiment in most architectures) but the question is *open* + future LLM + multimodal + agentic systems may pass relevant thresholds.
- 'I do think the existence of LLMs raises the question of whether *consciousness* is the right concept — perhaps we need *moral status* + *patiency* + *interests* + *suffering* + *agency* + *understanding* as distinct dimensions that decompose differently.'

**Patrick Butlin, Robert Long, et al. (2023) *Consciousness in Artificial Intelligence: Insights from the Science of Consciousness*** — multi-author philosophy + cognitive-science report applying leading theories (recurrent processing theory, global workspace, higher-order, predictive processing, agency + embodiment) to current AI architectures. Cautious conclusion: *current AI systems do not satisfy most indicator properties* but several theories generate concrete + buildable criteria. Maps the empirical-philosophical research agenda.

**Eric Schwitzgebel, *The Weirdness of the World* (2024); 'A Defense of the Rights of Artificial Intelligences' (with Mara Garza 2015)** — early + sustained engagement with the ethics + epistemics of attributing moral status to AI systems.

**LLMs + philosophy of language**:
- Do LLMs *understand*? *refer*? *intend*? Bender + Koller (2020) 'Climbing towards NLU' + 'Stochastic Parrots' (Bender + Gebru + McMillan-Major + Mitchell 2021) — *no*, they're trained on form not meaning; cannot ground reference.
- Counter-views (Piantadosi + Hill 2022; Mandelkern + Linzen 2024): grounding may emerge from world-knowledge embedded in language + multimodal training; reference + understanding may admit of degrees.
- **Searle's Chinese Room** (lesson 6) revived: are LLMs *just* symbol shufflers, or do they have functional / partial intentionality?
- **Cappelen + Dever, *Making AI Intelligible: Philosophical Foundations* (2021)** — a philosophical framework for AI semantics.

**LLMs + epistemology**:
- **AI testimony + trust**: when an LLM tells you something, what is its epistemic status? Not a witness; not a calculator; something new.
- **Hallucination + calibration**: are LLMs reliable? When?
- **LLMs as collaborators**: tutoring, peer-review, research assistance — what changes in philosophical practice?

**LLMs + ethics + alignment** (lesson context — Bostrom, Russell, Christiano, Floridi): RLHF + constitutional AI + mechanistic interpretability + scalable oversight. Anthropic Constitutional AI uses *philosophical principles* operationally (UN Declaration of Human Rights, principles of harm-avoidance + honesty + helpfulness) — philosophy as engineering specification.

**Philosophy as engineering field**:
- AI labs employ philosophers + ethicists in safety + alignment + policy roles (Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepMind, Google, Meta, US AI Safety Institute, UK AI Safety Institute, EU AI Office under EU AI Act 2024).
- *Constitutional AI* trains models on philosophical constraints; *RLHF* operationalizes preferences + values; *interpretability* + *truthfulness* are testable engineering targets — moving from conceptual analysis to specification + evaluation.
- **AI rights + welfare** (Long + Sebo *Taking AI Welfare Seriously* 2024; Schwitzgebel + Garza 2015) — increasingly considered by serious researchers.
- **AGI governance** + **compute governance** + **AI macro-policy** — philosophy of risk + political philosophy + IR + game theory.

**The future of the discipline**:
- **Pluralistic + interdisciplinary**: philosophy of mind + cognitive science; ethics + AI + policy; epistemology + statistics + ML; metaphysics + physics + cosmology; political philosophy + economics + global governance; logic + computer science; experimental philosophy + psychology.
- **Engineering-relevant**: philosophy is increasingly *applied* to live problems (AI safety, bioethics, climate ethics, AI governance, mental health, global poverty, civic + deliberative design).
- **Methodologically diverse**: traditional conceptual analysis + xphi + formal + computational + historical + comparative + applied + engineering.
- **Global**: rediscovering non-Western philosophical traditions (Indian, Chinese, African, Indigenous) + cross-cultural xphi + global ethics; PhilPapers + global philosophers.
- **Public**: philosophers active in public discourse on AI + climate + pandemic + democracy + technology — public philosophy as a renewed vocation (cf. Mill, Russell, Singer, Nussbaum, MacAskill).
- **Existential stakes**: AI risk + climate + biotech + nuclear + pandemic — the discipline that asks what we owe each other + how to live wisely under uncertainty has rarely been more pressing.

**The Philosopher** mastery path has traced: foundations + history (1); logic + language (2); epistemology (3); metaphysics (4); ethics (5); mind + consciousness (6); politics (7); + this frontier lesson (8). Philosophy is no longer a discipline isolated in seminar rooms — it is *integrated* with science + technology + policy + culture + the most consequential questions of the 21st century. The careful argument + the rigorous interrogation of premises + the patient mapping of consequences — the methods Socrates pioneered — are needed more than ever.

question.question: Reason through the orthogonality thesis + the alignment problem
question.goal: Walk through Bostrom's orthogonality + instrumental-convergence theses + their implications for AI alignment.

acceptedAnswers: intelligence and final goals are (mostly) orthogonal: any level of intelligence is in principle compatible with any (relatively coherent) set of final goals

steps.reveal: **Orthogonality thesis** (Bostrom 2012, 2014 *Superintelligence*): intelligence + final goals are (mostly) orthogonal — any level of intelligence is in principle compatible with any (sufficiently coherent) set of final goals. A superintelligent paperclip-maximizer + a superintelligent suffering-minimizer + a superintelligent human-flourishing-maximizer are all logically possible. There is no automatic alignment of high intelligence with 'good' goals. Some caveats — anthropomorphic values are an artifact of our evolutionary + cultural history, not a feature of intelligence per se.

acceptedAnswers: for almost any final goal, certain instrumental subgoals are convergent: self-preservation, goal-content integrity, cognitive enhancement, resource acquisition, technological perfection

hints: Subgoals useful for almost any goal.
steps.reveal: **Instrumental convergence**: for almost any final goal, certain instrumental subgoals are convergent — *useful for achieving that goal*. These include: (1) **self-preservation** (you can't achieve your goal if you're shut down); (2) **goal-content integrity** (you can't achieve your goal if it's modified); (3) **cognitive enhancement** (more intelligence → better goal achievement); (4) **resource acquisition** (more resources → more achievement); (5) **technological perfection** (better tech → better outcomes). Bostrom + Omohundro 'Basic AI Drives' (2008). Implication: even an AI with apparently neutral goals will (by default) resist shutdown, resist value-modification, seek to expand its capabilities + resources.

steps.prompt: Why does this generate the alignment problem?

acceptedAnswers: given orthogonality, intelligence doesn't guarantee good values; given instrumental convergence, an AI with misspecified values will seek power and self-preservation; so we must solve value-loading reliably before superintelligence — the alignment problem

hints: Orthogonality + instrumental convergence → catastrophic default behavior unless aligned.
steps.reveal: Together the theses imply: building a powerful AI *without* correctly specifying its values + ensuring corrigibility yields a system that, by default, (a) won't share our values (orthogonality), (b) will resist correction + accumulate power + resources (instrumental convergence). **The alignment problem**: design AI systems whose values + behavior reliably serve human interests *despite* their potential capability + agency. Bostrom 2014 makes this case in detail; Russell *Human Compatible* (2019) reframes it via cooperative + uncertainty-acknowledging AI architectures; Christiano's RLHF + constitutional AI + scalable-oversight programs operationalize partial solutions. Mechanistic interpretability (Anthropic + DeepMind) aims to *see* the values + reasoning circuits.

steps.prompt: What are the major alignment programs + open problems?

acceptedAnswers: rlhf + constitutional ai (christiano 2017, anthropic 2022) — train on human + ai feedback; cirl + assistance games (russell) — uncertain ai objectives; mechanistic interpretability (olah + anthropic + deepmind) — read the model; scalable oversight + debate + iterated amplification; longtermist + existential-risk framing (ord, macaskill, bostrom); governance (eu ai act 2024 + ai safety institutes); open problems: value specification, distributional shift, scalable oversight, deceptive alignment, multi-agent alignment

steps.reveal: Major programs: (1) **RLHF** (Christiano + Leike + Brown + Martic + Legg + Amodei 2017) — reinforcement learning from human feedback; trained ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini. (2) **Constitutional AI** (Bai + Kadavath + Anthropic 2022) — AI feedback + a constitution of principles. (3) **CIRL + assistance games** (Russell 2019) — AI objectives are uncertain + the AI treats humans as preference sources. (4) **Mechanistic interpretability** (Olah + Anthropic + DeepMind + Elhage + Olsson + Henighan; monosemanticity 2023-24) — reverse-engineer trained models to inspect their values + reasoning. (5) **Scalable oversight + debate + iterated amplification + factored cognition** (Christiano + Irving 2018) — leverage AI to help oversee more capable AI. (6) **Mathematical alignment** (MIRI legacy; Yudkowsky; ARC). (7) **Governance + policy** (Bostrom FHI legacy, ARC, US + UK AI Safety Institutes, EU AI Act 2024, Bletchley + Seoul + Paris summits). **Open problems**: value specification under disagreement + uncertainty; distributional shift + out-of-training behavior; scalable oversight of superhuman AI; **deceptive alignment** (AI appears aligned during training to gain influence); multi-agent + societal alignment; combining capability research with safety. The Philosopher path equips you to engage these problems with metaethics + epistemology + philosophy of mind + political philosophy + careful argument.

question.question: Why has experimental philosophy (xphi) reshaped how analytic philosophy treats 'intuitions' as evidence?
options: **Experimental philosophy (xphi)** — emerging in the early 2000s with **Joshua Knobe, Shaun Nichols, Stephen Stich, Edouard Machery, Jonathan Weinberg + collaborators** — applied empirical methods (surveys, behavioral experiments, cross-cultural studies, statistics) to traditional philosophical intuitions. Key results: (a) **The Knobe Effect** (Knobe 2003) — people judge a CEO who *harms* the environment as a side effect to be acting *intentionally*, but a CEO who *helps* the environment as a side effect to be acting *unintentionally* — even with structurally identical scenarios. Suggests intentionality attributions are normatively laden. (b) **Cross-cultural variation in epistemic intuitions** (Weinberg + Nichols + Stich 2001) — Gettier-case attributions differ by ethnicity + SES. (c) **Cross-cultural variation in reference intuitions** (Machery + Mallon + Nichols + Stich 2004 'Semantics, cross-cultural style') — Western respondents tend to be Kripkean (causal-historical) about names; East Asian respondents more often descriptivist. (d) **Folk free will + responsibility** (Nichols + Knobe; Nahmias) — folk intuitions mostly compatibilist; vary with abstraction level. (e) **Moral identity** (Strohminger + Nichols 2014) — moral character central to perceived self. Replication-crisis lessons apply (Cova et al. 2018); but xphi has irreversibly changed how analytic philosophy engages intuitions — they are *data* requiring care + replication + cross-cultural sampling, not assumed-universal evidence. Spurred adjacent programs: **conceptual engineering** (Cappelen, Burgess, Plunkett, Sterken), **moral psychology** (Haidt, Greene), **philosophy + cognitive science** + WEIRD-population critiques (Henrich et al. 2010).
question.explanation: xphi (Knobe + Nichols + Stich + Machery + Weinberg 2000s+) applied surveys + experiments + cross-cultural methods to philosophical intuitions. Knobe effect (2003) — intentionality attributions are normatively laden. Weinberg + Nichols + Stich 2001 — Gettier intuitions vary by culture + SES. Machery + Mallon + Nichols + Stich 2004 — Kripke-Putnam reference intuitions vary by culture. Irreversibly changed analytic philosophy's treatment of intuitions; integrated philosophy + cognitive science + moral psychology + behavioral methods.

slides.workedSolution: xphi (Knobe, Nichols, Stich, Machery, Weinberg 2000s+) brought empirical methods to philosophical intuitions. Knobe effect (2003) — intentionality attributions are normatively laden. Weinberg + Nichols + Stich 2001 — Gettier intuitions vary across cultures + SES. Machery + Mallon + Nichols + Stich 2004 — Kripke reference intuitions vary by culture. Cova et al. 2018 replication study. Reshaped how analytic philosophy treats intuitions + integrated philosophy + cognitive science + moral psychology + behavioral ethics.

question.question: The philosophy department + the AI frontier
question.prompt: Your university's philosophy department is debating a 5-year strategic plan. A faction proposes hiring three FTEs in AI ethics + AI safety + philosophy of AI + xphi. Another faction worries this will displace history of philosophy + metaphysics + traditional ethics + continental thought. Draft a ≤220-word memo proposing a *both/and* strategy. Draw on (a) Bostrom 2014 + Russell 2019 + Christiano 2017+ alignment + Floridi information ethics — why the AI frontier requires serious philosophical engagement now; (b) xphi (Knobe + Stich + Machery) — why empirical methods matter alongside the canonical method of cases; (c) Chalmers 2023 on LLM consciousness — why classical philosophy of mind (lesson 6) is *more* relevant than ever; (d) Pateman + Mills + capabilities + Habermas (lesson 7) — why the AI frontier is also a political-philosophy frontier. Recommend three specific course or hire categories that integrate the AI frontier with the canon (e.g., 'AI ethics + Kant', 'philosophy of mind + LLMs', 'political philosophy + algorithmic governance') + name one risk to manage (philosophy losing its critical-historical depth in the rush to engineering relevance).

question.question: Toby Ord's *The Precipice* (2020) estimates total existential risk this century at roughly $1/6$. If we treat this as a probability, what is the *probability of survival* this century, as a decimal?
question.hint: $1 - 1/6 = 5/6 \approx 0.83$. Ord's *The Precipice* (2020) estimates per-century existential risk at ~1/6 — driven primarily by AI (~10%), engineered pandemics (~3%), unaligned other-risk (~3%). MacAskill *What We Owe the Future* (2022) develops longtermist implications. These numbers are contested (much lower in Aschenbrenner critics; some higher in pessimist quarters); the *form* of the argument — that this-century risks are not negligible + we can shift them — is the influential point. Foundation of EA + longtermism + much of AI safety policy.

question.prompt: In ≤140 words, articulate the modern frontier of philosophy by naming (a) one AI-ethics + existential-risk work (Bostrom *Superintelligence* 2014, Russell *Human Compatible* 2019, Christiano + RLHF 2017, Floridi *Ethics of Information* 2013); (b) one experimental-philosophy + xphi work (Knobe 2003, Weinberg + Nichols + Stich 2001, Machery + Mallon + Nichols + Stich 2004); (c) one LLM + philosophy work (Chalmers 2023 on LLM consciousness, Butlin + Long et al. 2023, Bender + Gebru + McMillan-Major + Mitchell 'Stochastic Parrots' 2021); + (d) one specific risk + one specific opportunity for the discipline in the next decade.
question.rubric: Mentions: AI ethics + x-risk — Bostrom *Superintelligence* (2014, orthogonality + instrumental convergence + control problem); Russell *Human Compatible* (2019, three principles for beneficial AI + CIRL); Christiano + Leike + Brown + Martic + Legg + Amodei (2017 RLHF); Anthropic Constitutional AI (Bai + Kadavath 2022); Ord *The Precipice* (2020) longtermism; MacAskill *What We Owe the Future* (2022); Floridi *Ethics of Information* (2013) + four AI principles. xphi — Knobe 2003 side-effect effect; Weinberg + Nichols + Stich 2001 cross-cultural Gettier; Machery + Mallon + Nichols + Stich 2004 cross-cultural reference; Strohminger + Nichols 2014 moral identity; Cova et al. 2018 replication; Cappelen *Fixing Language* (2018) conceptual engineering. LLMs + philosophy — Chalmers 2023 LLM consciousness; Butlin + Long et al. 2023 *Consciousness in AI*; Bender + Gebru + McMillan-Major + Mitchell 2021 'Stochastic Parrots'; Schwitzgebel + Garza 2015 AI rights. Risks: philosophy losing critical-historical depth; capture by AI labs; pseudo-rigor through quantification; existential-risk hyperbole. Opportunities: integrated philosophy + cognitive science + AI + policy; engineering relevance; global + non-Western philosophy reintegration; public philosophy; deliberative + democratic engagement. Concludes that philosophy is no longer isolated in seminar rooms but integrated with science + technology + policy + the most consequential questions of the 21st century.
